ontology.note: Emits an fw:NetworkReachability activity carrying fw:originCount, fw:reachedNodeCount, fw:travelBudgetMetres, fw:travelBudgetMinutes, fw:assumedSpeedMetresPerMinute, fw:travelMode, fw:travelDirection, fw:edgeLengthSource and, when origins were left out or routed across unmapped ground, fw:unconnectedSiteCount, fw:unconnectedSites, fw:offNetworkSiteCount and fw:offNetworkSites, and prov:used the site source.

changes.description: Street junctions within a travel budget of an origin, each carrying the budget left on arrival. Extracted from the Dijkstra inside isochrone (src/catchments.ts:76) unchanged, including the edge reversal that makes inbound a different question from outbound. Fourth of six primitives an isochrone composition needs. Settles the carrier question that stopped the decomposition in experiment 82: the truncation downstream consumes budget minus cost at the edge's start node, which is a per-node quantity, so reached junctions travel as points with a remainingM attribute and no lines port type is needed. The corridor step that follows truncates by remainingM over lengthM and never restates the minutes or the speed. Takes no UTM zone, unlike the eight metric widgets: costs are the network's own lengthM values and nothing here re-measures geometry. Travel mode is an explicit parameter -- walking, cycling, driving or other -- checked against the speed, because the 75 metres per minute this project defaulted to everywhere is 4.5 km/h from Advanced-1 NB03 cell 10, where it is an assumption about pedestrians in Soho in 1854 and was being inherited rather than chosen. Public transport is refused as a mode, because it follows routes and a timetable rather than the street network. See docs/experiments/83-reachable-junctions.md.

Each reached junction now carries travelDirection beside remainingM. The corridor step that follows has to truncate edges the same way round as the traversal ran, and direction was a parameter of this node that its output did not state -- so the corridor would have needed its own direction parameter, free to contradict this one. Carrying it as data closes that, for the same reason remainingM is carried rather than the budget. Additive: no existing attribute changed.

Each reached junction now carries speedMPerMin and travelMode. travel_time_band has to convert its minutes into metres, and the speed was a parameter of this node that its output did not state -- so the band would have needed its own speed parameter, free to contradict this one, which is the defect the mode plausibility bands exist to catch. Carrying it as data closes it, for the same reason remainingM and travelDirection are carried. Additive: no existing attribute changed.

The walk from the site onto the network is charged against the budget. It was measured, attached to the point and then spent by nothing, so every reachable set reached further than its time allowed. An origin whose walk alone spends the budget now reaches nothing and is reported rather than silently returning an empty set. Junctions also carry the origin’s own coordinates and its snap distance, so whatever draws a corridor can draw the first leg of the route. Experiment 114.

evidence.note: Eleven unit checks cover junctions inside a 200 m budget being returned and a 300 m one not; travelled plus remaining equalling the budget at every junction; the cheapest route deciding the cost, where a 400 m direct street loses to 100 plus 100 through a third junction; inbound and outbound differing on a one-way street in both directions; an origin without a networkNodeId failing with a message naming the snap step; an origin snapped to a different network being refused rather than dropped; per-origin sets tagged by origin; the constant speed and the trusted street lengths both appearing in the notes; a node beyond the budget being discovered but never settled; refusal of an impossible budget, speed, direction or label; a speed outside its mode's plausible band being refused in both directions, where 400 m/min labelled walking is reported as 24 km/h against a 1.8 to 6.6 km/h band; the 1854 Soho 75 m/min sitting inside the walking band, since that is where the band came from; public transport being refused with its reason; and the mode and the km/h travelling in both the notes and the receipt. One check runs the real composition: snapping then reachability over the 738-node Soho network the John Snow example ships, at its own 5 minutes and 75 m per minute, reaching 142 junctions. Not established: that the reached set is what anyone can actually reach. Parity against NetworkX ego_graph with distance='length' is not done.
